## The prediction task

**Goal:** predict the quantity sold in a stock observation from the information recorded for that observation.

| Input | How the model uses it |
|:---|:---|
| SKU and category | Categorical features with learned embeddings |
| Price, order, duration | Numeric features transformed using training-data statistics |

The dataset contains **500,000 stock observations**. The target is quantity sold, measured in units.

## Evaluation design

| Split | Observations | Purpose |
|:---|---:|:---|
| Training | 349,975 | Fit model weights and preprocessing |
| Validation | 74,736 | Compare models and select the epoch |
| Test | 75,289 | Evaluate the selected model once |

Observations were split at random. A SKU can appear in more than one split, so the test set primarily measures performance on **new observations**, not new products.

## How the model trains

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\Large CSV chunk $\rightarrow$ mini-batches $\rightarrow$ weight updates
\end{center}
```

| Unit | Size | Role |
|:---|---:|:---|
| Chunk | 16,384 rows | Limits how much CSV data is held in memory |
| Mini-batch | 1,024 rows | Sets the number of examples per weight update |

Each epoch makes another pass through the training observations. The two sizes serve different purposes: memory control and optimization.

## Network and preprocessing

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\Large Inputs $\rightarrow$ 256 $\rightarrow$ 128 $\rightarrow$ 64 $\rightarrow$ predicted quantity
\end{center}
```

- SKU and category are categorical; numeric variables are standardized from the training split.
- The three hidden layers use sigmoid activations. Training uses Adam and mean squared error.
- The selected model uses an exponential output link, which yields nonnegative predictions.

## Held-out test performance

| Model / split | $R^2$ | RMSE | MAE |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| Training | 0.6562 | 29.61 | 12.26 |
| Validation | 0.6105 | 31.06 | 12.96 |
| **Test** | **0.6127** | **31.90** | **13.19** |
| Test mean-only baseline | $\approx 0$ | 51.25 | 24.83 |

The selected model explains about **61% of variation** in held-out observation quantity. RMSE and MAE are in units sold.

## What the test result does not show

- **New products:** SKUs can repeat across splits. Only 5,008 test observations use the unseen-SKU bucket.
- **Future forecasts:** the split is random, not chronological.
- **At-order predictions:** duration may only be known after an observation ends.
- **Small-error guarantees:** large quantity errors weigh heavily in MSE and $R^2$.

## Main findings

1. The model reaches **test $R^2=0.6127$** and **RMSE = 31.90 units**, outperforming a mean-only baseline.
2. During the selected trial, sampled process memory peaked near **604 MB** on the CPU run.
3. The reported score applies to randomly held-out stock observations. A time-based or unseen-product test would answer a different question.
